Cookie Policy

Cookie Policy

This Cookie Policy explains how Booming Venture uses cookies, pixels, scripts, tags, local storage and similar technologies on https://boomingventure.com.

Last updated 20 May 2026
Website https://boomingventure.com
Contact info@boomingventure.com
Plain English summary

Booming Venture uses cookies to make the website work, protect the website, understand website performance and, if you give consent, measure marketing and advertising performance.

Necessary cookies are used because the website cannot work properly without them. Analytics cookies may be used to improve the website. Marketing and tracking cookies are only used after your consent where consent is required.

Important: this Cookie Policy must match the actual cookie banner and the actual tools active on the website. If Booming Venture adds Google Analytics, Google Tag Manager, LinkedIn Insight Tag, Meta Pixel, Google Ads tracking, Microsoft Clarity, Hotjar, Calendly, HubSpot, Brevo tracking, YouTube embeds, Vimeo embeds or similar tools, this policy and the cookie consent setup must be reviewed.

Contents

1. What are cookies? 2. Who we are 3. Why we use cookies 4. Types of cookies we use 5. Legal basis 6. Cookie overview 7. Third-party cookies 8. Marketing and tracking cookies 9. Analytics cookies 10. Embedded content 11. Managing cookie preferences 12. Browser settings 13. Cookie retention 14. Changes 15. Implementation checklist 16. Contact

1. What are cookies?

Cookies are small text files stored on your device when you visit a website. They can help a website remember your preferences, keep the website secure, understand how visitors use the website, or measure marketing performance.

Similar technologies include pixels, tags, scripts, local storage, session storage, software development kits and tracking identifiers.

In this Cookie Policy, the word “cookies” also refers to these similar technologies.

2. Who we are

Booming Venture is an AI-powered growth and marketing consultancy based in Rotterdam, The Netherlands.

Organisation Booming Venture
Website https://boomingventure.com
Address Breedveldsingel 1, Rotterdam, The Netherlands
Chamber of Commerce number 96442018
VAT number NL005211648B76
Email info@boomingventure.com

For questions about cookies, contact us at info@boomingventure.com.

3. Why we use cookies

We may use cookies for the following purposes:

  • To make the website work properly
  • To remember cookie preferences
  • To keep the website secure
  • To prevent spam, abuse and fraud
  • To process forms and website requests
  • To understand how visitors use the website
  • To improve website speed, structure, content and user experience
  • To measure marketing campaigns if you give consent
  • To measure ad conversions if you give consent
  • To support retargeting or remarketing if you give consent
  • To show embedded content where technically needed and where legally allowed

4. Types of cookies we use

4.1 Necessary cookies

Necessary cookies are required for the website to work. These cookies support basic functions such as page loading, form submission, security, spam prevention, login sessions, cookie preference storage and website administration.

These cookies do not require consent, but we still inform you about them.

4.2 Preference cookies

Preference cookies remember choices you make, such as language settings, display preferences or cookie choices.

Some preference cookies may be necessary if they are required to provide a function you requested. Other preference cookies may require consent depending on how they are used.

4.3 Analytics cookies

Analytics cookies help us understand how visitors use the website. For example, they can show which pages are visited, how long visitors stay and which content is useful.

We only use analytics cookies without consent if they are configured in a privacy-friendly way and have little or no impact on privacy. If analytics cookies are used for tracking, advertising, profiling or cross-site identification, we ask for consent first.

4.4 Marketing and tracking cookies

Marketing and tracking cookies may be used to measure advertising performance, track conversions, build audiences, show relevant ads, retarget visitors or understand campaign performance across websites.

These cookies are only placed after your consent where consent is required.

4.5 Embedded content cookies

Embedded content from third-party services, such as videos, maps, booking widgets or social media posts, may place cookies. Where required, we block such content until you give consent.

5. Legal basis for cookies

We use necessary cookies because they are needed for the website to work and for security.

We may use privacy-friendly analytics cookies based on legitimate interest where legally allowed and where the privacy impact is low.

We only use tracking cookies, advertising cookies and non-essential marketing cookies after consent where consent is required.

Cookie category Legal basis Consent needed?
Necessary cookies Necessary website operation and legitimate interest in security No
Preference cookies Consent or necessary website function, depending on use Sometimes
Privacy-friendly analytics cookies Legitimate interest, where legally allowed Not always
Analytics cookies with tracking or advertising use Consent Yes
Marketing and tracking cookies Consent Yes
Third-party embedded content cookies Consent where required Often yes

6. Cookie overview

The exact cookies on our website depend on the tools that are active. The table below explains the main cookie categories that may apply on BoomingVenture.com.

Category Possible providers Purpose Examples of data Consent
Necessary cookies WordPress, hosting provider, security tools, cookie consent tool Website operation, security, form handling, admin sessions, cookie preference storage Session ID, cookie preference, technical logs, IP address No
Form and spam protection cookies Contact Form 7, reCAPTCHA, Akismet or similar tools Form submission, spam prevention, website abuse prevention IP address, browser data, form behaviour, submitted form data Depends on tool and setup
Analytics cookies Google Analytics, Microsoft Clarity or privacy-friendly analytics tools Website statistics, content improvement, user experience analysis Page visits, device type, browser, approximate location, interaction data Depends on privacy impact and setup
Marketing cookies Google Ads, LinkedIn Insight Tag, Meta Pixel or similar platforms Conversion tracking, remarketing, campaign measurement, audience building Cookie IDs, page visits, campaign source, conversion events Yes
Email and CRM cookies Brevo, HubSpot or similar platforms Lead capture, email subscription, CRM follow-up, campaign reporting Email status, form submission, campaign engagement, contact profile data Depends on use. Marketing tracking requires consent where required.
Booking cookies Calendly, Google Calendar, Microsoft Bookings or similar tools Booking calls, scheduling meetings, showing calendar availability Name, email, time zone, meeting details, device data Depends on embed and setup
Embedded content cookies YouTube, Vimeo, Google Maps, LinkedIn, X, other social or media platforms Showing videos, maps, social posts or external content Device data, viewing behaviour, cookie IDs, interaction data Often yes

This table is category-based. A live cookie scan should be used to create the final exact cookie list with cookie name, provider, purpose, category and retention period.

7. Third-party cookies

Some cookies may be placed by third-party providers. These providers may process data according to their own privacy and cookie policies.

Third-party cookies may come from analytics tools, advertising platforms, embedded videos, maps, CRM tools, booking tools, email marketing tools, social media platforms or spam protection tools.

We try to limit third-party cookies where possible. Where legally required, third-party cookies are only loaded after consent.

8. Marketing and tracking cookies

Marketing and tracking cookies are used to follow visitors across websites, measure advertising campaigns, retarget visitors, build audiences or connect website behaviour to advertising platforms.

Examples of tools that may place marketing or tracking cookies are:

  • Google Ads conversion tracking
  • Google Tag Manager with marketing tags
  • LinkedIn Insight Tag
  • Meta Pixel
  • HubSpot tracking
  • Brevo marketing tracking
  • Other advertising or retargeting platforms

These cookies are only placed after your consent where consent is required.

Marketing cookies must not load before consent. This includes hidden pixels, remarketing tags, conversion tags and scripts loaded through Google Tag Manager or similar tag managers.

9. Analytics cookies

Analytics cookies help us understand how visitors use BoomingVenture.com. This helps us improve content, user experience, page structure, lead generation and website performance.

Analytics can be used without consent only when the setup is privacy-friendly and has little or no impact on visitor privacy.

A privacy-friendly analytics setup should normally include:

  • No sharing of analytics data for advertising
  • No cross-site tracking
  • Limited data retention
  • No unnecessary user identification
  • IP anonymisation where available
  • No combination with advertising profiles
  • A proper processor agreement where required

If analytics is used for advertising, profiling, remarketing or cross-site tracking, we ask for consent first.

10. Embedded content

Our website may contain embedded content from third-party websites, such as videos, maps, social media posts, podcasts, forms or booking widgets.

Embedded content behaves as if you visited the external website directly. These third parties may collect data, place cookies and track your interaction with the embedded content.

Where required, we block embedded content until you give consent.

11. Managing cookie preferences

You can manage your cookie preferences through the cookie banner or cookie settings on our website.

You can choose between different cookie categories, such as necessary cookies, analytics cookies and marketing cookies.

You can withdraw or change your consent at any time through the cookie settings.

Recommended website button text: “Cookie settings”.

Place this link in the footer so visitors can change consent later.

12. Browser settings

You can also block or delete cookies through your browser settings.

Most browsers allow you to:

  • Delete existing cookies
  • Block all cookies
  • Block third-party cookies
  • Receive a warning before cookies are placed
  • Clear cookies when closing the browser

If you block necessary cookies, parts of the website may not work properly.

13. Cookie retention

Cookies can be session cookies or persistent cookies.

  • Session cookies are deleted when you close your browser.
  • Persistent cookies remain on your device for a set period or until you delete them.

Cookie retention depends on the provider, tool and purpose. We aim to use the shortest reasonable retention period.

Cookie type Typical retention Reason
Session cookies Until browser session ends Basic website operation
Cookie preference cookies Usually 6 to 12 months Remembering your cookie choice
Security cookies Usually session-based or short-term Security, spam prevention and abuse detection
Analytics cookies Depends on provider and configuration Website measurement and improvement
Marketing cookies Depends on provider and configuration Campaign measurement, retargeting and advertising

14. Changes to this Cookie Policy

We may update this Cookie Policy when our website, tools, cookies, consent setup or legal obligations change.

The latest version will always be available on this page. The date at the top shows when this Cookie Policy was last updated.

15. Implementation checklist for Booming Venture

This checklist helps make sure this Cookie Policy matches the real website setup.

15.1 Cookie banner requirements

  • Show Accept and Reject on the first layer
  • Make Reject as easy to find as Accept
  • Do not use pre-ticked boxes
  • Do not load marketing cookies before consent
  • Do not load tracking pixels before consent
  • Allow granular choices by cookie category
  • Store proof of consent
  • Allow users to change or withdraw consent later
  • Add a “Cookie settings” link in the footer

15.2 Tools to check

Run a cookie scan and check whether these tools are active:

  • WordPress
  • Hosting provider cookies
  • Security plugin cookies
  • Cookie consent plugin cookies
  • Contact Form 7
  • reCAPTCHA
  • Akismet
  • Google Analytics
  • Google Tag Manager
  • Google Ads conversion tracking
  • LinkedIn Insight Tag
  • Meta Pixel
  • Microsoft Clarity
  • Hotjar
  • Brevo forms or tracking
  • HubSpot forms or tracking
  • Calendly embeds
  • YouTube embeds
  • Vimeo embeds
  • Google Maps embeds

15.3 Final cookie table to complete after scan

After scanning the live website, create a final cookie table with:

  • Cookie name
  • Provider
  • Purpose
  • Category
  • Retention period
  • Whether consent is required

Do not manually guess the exact cookies. Use a real cookie scan after the cookie banner and all tracking tools are installed.

16. Contact

For questions about this Cookie Policy or how Booming Venture uses cookies, contact:

Booming Venture
Breedveldsingel 1
Rotterdam, The Netherlands
Chamber of Commerce: 96442018
VAT: NL005211648B76

Email: info@boomingventure.com
Website: https://boomingventure.com

privacy-policy.raw:
Privacy Policy and Cookie Policy

Privacy Policy

This Privacy Policy explains how Booming Venture collects, uses, stores and protects personal data when you visit our website, contact us, download content, book a call, use our forms, subscribe to updates, or work with us.

Last updated 20 May 2026
Website https://boomingventure.com
Contact info@boomingventure.com
Plain English summary

Booming Venture handles personal data carefully, transparently and only for clear business purposes. We do not sell personal data. We do not intentionally collect sensitive personal data. We use data to run our website, respond to requests, deliver services, improve our marketing, protect our systems and meet legal obligations.

This policy is written for website visitors, prospects, clients, suppliers, partners and other business contacts of Booming Venture.

This Privacy Policy must match the actual website setup. If Booming Venture adds new forms, cookies, analytics tools, advertising pixels, CRM tools, AI tools, booking tools or plugins, this policy and the cookie settings must be reviewed.

Contents

1. Who we are 2. What personal data we collect 3. How we collect personal data 4. Why we use personal data 5. Legal bases 6. B2B lead generation 7. Forms and lead magnets 8. Email marketing 9. Cookie Policy 10. Tools and service providers 11. AI tools and automation 12. International transfers 13. Retention periods 14. Security 15. Data breaches 16. Your privacy rights 17. Complaints 18. Implementation checklist 19. Contact

1. Who we are

Booming Venture is an AI-powered growth and marketing consultancy based in Rotterdam, The Netherlands.

Organisation Booming Venture
Website https://boomingventure.com
Address Breedveldsingel 1, Rotterdam, The Netherlands
Chamber of Commerce number 96442018
VAT number NL005211648B76
Email info@boomingventure.com

For the personal data described in this Privacy Policy, Booming Venture is the controller, unless clearly stated otherwise.

2. What personal data we collect

We only collect personal data when this is necessary for our website, communication, marketing, security, administration, legal obligations or delivery of services.

2.1 Contact details

When you contact us, fill in a form, book a call, request a proposal, subscribe to updates, or download content, we may collect:

  • Name
  • Business email address
  • Phone number
  • Company name
  • Job title
  • Website URL
  • LinkedIn profile URL, if you provide it
  • Message content
  • Preferred contact method
  • Any other information you choose to provide

2.2 Business and project information

When you ask for advice, a proposal, a strategy session, an audit, a quickscan, or a project, we may process:

  • Company information
  • Marketing, sales, AI or growth challenges
  • Website and funnel information
  • Campaign information
  • CRM or pipeline information you choose to share
  • Business goals
  • Meeting notes
  • Project requirements
  • Proposal and contract information
  • Communication history

2.3 Website and technical data

When you visit our website, we may process technical data such as:

  • IP address
  • Browser type
  • Device type
  • Operating system
  • Pages visited
  • Referring website
  • Date and time of visit
  • Approximate location based on IP address
  • Cookie preferences
  • Interaction data, such as clicks and page behaviour, if analytics or tracking tools are enabled

2.4 Marketing and newsletter data

If you subscribe to updates, download a resource, register for an event, or give permission to receive marketing communication, we may process:

  • Name
  • Email address
  • Company name
  • Role or job title
  • Business interests
  • Subscription status
  • Email opens and clicks, where legally allowed
  • Consent records
  • Unsubscribe records

2.5 Client administration data

If you become a client, supplier, partner, or contractor, we may process:

  • Contact details
  • Company details
  • Billing details
  • Payment information
  • Invoice history
  • Contracts
  • Project communication
  • Tax and accounting information

2.6 Comments or user generated content

If our website allows comments or user generated content, we may collect the data shown in the form, IP address, browser user agent, comment content and submission date.

This may be used for spam detection, moderation and website security.

Booming Venture may disable public comments if they are not needed. This reduces privacy risk, spam risk and security risk.

2.7 Sensitive data

We do not intentionally collect special categories of personal data, such as health data, political opinions, religious beliefs, trade union membership, biometric data, or criminal offence data.

Please do not send us sensitive personal data unless this is strictly necessary and we have agreed this with you in advance.

3. How we collect personal data

We collect personal data in the following ways:

  • Directly from you when you fill in a form
  • Directly from you when you email, call or message us
  • Directly from you during meetings, workshops or projects
  • Automatically through website cookies and similar technologies
  • Through analytics, CRM, email marketing, booking and security tools
  • From public business sources, such as company websites, LinkedIn and public company registers, where relevant for B2B communication
  • From clients, partners or suppliers when needed for project work

We do not buy consumer databases. If we use B2B prospecting or outreach, we do this only where we have a lawful basis and where the communication is relevant to the recipient’s professional role.

4. Why we use personal data

4.1 To respond to requests

We use your data to respond when you contact us, request information, book a call, complete a form, request a proposal, or ask for advice.

4.2 To provide services

We use client and project data to deliver strategy, marketing, AI, automation, growth, training, consulting and implementation services.

4.3 To manage client relationships

We use personal data to manage communication, meetings, project planning, proposals, contracts, support, reporting and follow-up.

4.4 To improve our website and services

We may use website and interaction data to understand how people use our website, which content performs well, and how we can improve user experience, messaging, services and conversion.

4.5 To send marketing communication

We may use your contact details to send newsletters, updates, invitations, resources, insights or commercial messages, but only where this is legally allowed. You can unsubscribe at any time.

4.6 To run campaigns and measure performance

We may use data to measure the effectiveness of campaigns, lead magnets, forms, ads, website pages, emails and sales processes.

Tracking cookies or advertising cookies are only used after valid consent where required.

4.7 To secure the website

We use technical data to protect our website, detect abuse, prevent spam, block attacks and maintain security.

4.8 To comply with legal obligations

We process data when needed for tax, accounting, contract, compliance, legal claims, data subject requests or other legal obligations.

5. Legal bases for processing

We only process personal data when we have a legal basis under the General Data Protection Regulation. The main legal bases we use are consent, contract, legal obligation and legitimate interest.

Purpose Legal basis
Responding to contact forms and requests Legitimate interest or steps before a contract
Providing services to clients Performance of a contract
Sending proposals and managing sales conversations Legitimate interest or steps before a contract
Client administration and invoicing Contract and legal obligation
Tax and accounting records Legal obligation
Newsletter after opt-in Consent
Relevant B2B communication to professional contacts Legitimate interest, unless consent is required
Tracking cookies and advertising pixels Consent
Functional website cookies Necessary website operation or legitimate interest
Low-impact privacy-friendly analytics Legitimate interest, where allowed
Website security and spam prevention Legitimate interest
Legal claims or dispute handling Legitimate interest or legal obligation

Where we rely on legitimate interest, we balance our business interest against your privacy rights. We do not use legitimate interest where your rights and freedoms outweigh our interest.

6. B2B lead generation and business outreach

Booming Venture works in a business-to-business context. We may contact relevant business professionals about services, events, resources, audits, workshops or opportunities when the communication is relevant to their professional role.

For B2B outreach, we may use limited professional contact data, such as name, company, role, business email address, LinkedIn profile, company website and publicly available business information.

We do not target private consumers with mass marketing. We do not sell personal data. We do not use sensitive personal data for prospecting.

Every recipient can object to direct marketing at any time. If you object, we will stop using your data for direct marketing.

7. Forms, lead magnets, quickscans and calculators

When you use a form, calculator, quickscan, audit request, download, webinar form or booking form, we process the information you submit.

This may include your name, email address, company, website, phone number, role, business challenges and answers to form questions.

We use this data to deliver the requested resource, respond to your request, analyse your business question, prepare advice or a proposal, follow up commercially where relevant, and improve our services and content.

If the form includes marketing opt-in, we will use your data for marketing only if you have consented or where another legal basis applies.

Recommended form text

For contact forms, Booming Venture may use this text:

By submitting this form, you agree that Booming Venture may use your information to respond to your request. We handle your data according to our Privacy Policy.

For newsletter opt-in, Booming Venture should use a separate checkbox:

I agree to receive marketing emails from Booming Venture. I can unsubscribe at any time.

8. Email marketing

If you subscribe to our email updates, we use your email address to send you relevant content, insights, offers, event invitations and updates.

Every marketing email includes an unsubscribe option.

We may measure email opens, clicks and engagement to improve our communication, but only where this is legally allowed and configured properly.

We do not sell email lists.

9. Cookie Policy

Our website may use cookies, pixels, scripts, tags, local storage or similar technologies.

Cookies are small files stored on your device. Some cookies are necessary for the website to work. Others help us understand website usage, improve performance, personalise content, or measure marketing campaigns.

9.1 Necessary cookies

These cookies are needed for basic website functions, security, form handling, cookie preferences and page loading. They do not require consent, but we still explain them in this policy.

9.2 Analytics cookies

Analytics cookies help us understand how visitors use the website.

We only use analytics without consent if the privacy impact is low, the analytics setup is privacy-friendly, the data is not shared for advertising, and the data is not used for cross-site tracking. If analytics has more than a low privacy impact, we ask for consent first.

9.3 Marketing and tracking cookies

Marketing and tracking cookies may be used for ad performance measurement, remarketing, conversion tracking, campaign attribution, social media pixels, personalised advertising and audience building.

We only place these cookies after your consent where required.

9.4 Managing cookie preferences

You can change your cookie preferences through the cookie banner or cookie settings on our website.

You can also delete or block cookies through your browser settings. Some website features may not work properly if you block certain cookies.

9.5 Cookie banner requirements

Booming Venture aims to use a cookie consent tool that:

  • Blocks non-essential cookies before consent
  • Separates necessary, analytics and marketing cookies
  • Stores proof of consent
  • Makes rejecting cookies as easy as accepting cookies
  • Allows users to withdraw consent
  • Does not use pre-ticked boxes
  • Does not place tracking scripts before consent
  • Provides clear information about cookie purpose, provider and retention

9.6 Cookie overview

The exact cookies on our website depend on the tools that are active. The table below explains the main categories that may apply.

Category Examples of providers Purpose Consent required
Necessary cookies WordPress, hosting provider, security tools, cookie consent tool Website operation, security, form handling, cookie preferences No
Analytics cookies Google Analytics, Microsoft Clarity, privacy-friendly analytics tools Website statistics, page performance, user experience improvement Sometimes. Consent is needed if the setup is not privacy-friendly or has more than low privacy impact.
Marketing cookies Google Ads, LinkedIn Insight Tag, Meta Pixel, other advertising platforms Campaign measurement, retargeting, conversion tracking, audience building Yes
Embedded content cookies YouTube, Vimeo, Google Maps, social media embeds, calendar tools Showing external content, maps, videos, booking widgets or social content Depends on the provider and setup. Consent may be required before loading the embed.
Email and CRM cookies Brevo, HubSpot, CRM or email marketing tools Form processing, lead management, email subscription, campaign follow-up Depends on the function. Marketing tracking requires consent where required.

Important: if Booming Venture uses Google Tag Manager, Google Analytics, LinkedIn Insight Tag, Meta Pixel, Hotjar, Microsoft Clarity, Google Ads conversion tracking, YouTube embeds, Calendly embeds, HubSpot tracking, Brevo tracking or similar tools, those tools must be checked in the cookie consent setup. Non-essential tracking must not load before valid consent.

10. Tools and service providers

We may use trusted service providers to run our website, marketing, communication, analytics, CRM, automation, hosting, security, accounting and project delivery.

These providers may process personal data on our behalf. We only share data where necessary. Where required, we use data processing agreements with processors.

10.1 Types of providers we may use

  • Website hosting providers
  • WordPress plugins and website tools
  • Form plugins
  • Email marketing platforms
  • CRM systems
  • Analytics tools
  • Advertising platforms
  • Calendar booking tools
  • Payment or invoicing tools
  • Cloud storage providers
  • AI and automation tools
  • Security and spam prevention tools
  • Professional advisers, such as accountants or legal advisers

10.2 Tool overview

Depending on the active website setup and business operations, Booming Venture may use tools in the categories below. If a specific tool is not active, it should not be treated as active processing.

Tool category Possible tools Purpose Data involved
Website and CMS WordPress, website theme, website plugins Website publishing, content management, forms, technical operation Technical data, form data, admin data
Hosting and security Hosting provider, firewall, spam protection, backups Hosting, website security, backups, abuse prevention IP address, technical logs, website data
Forms Contact Form 7 or similar tools Processing contact requests, downloads, quickscans and lead forms Name, email, company, message, submitted answers
Email marketing Brevo or similar email tools Sending newsletters, updates and follow-up emails Name, email, company, subscription status, engagement data
Analytics Google Analytics, Microsoft Clarity or privacy-friendly analytics tools Website measurement, user experience improvement, content performance Technical data, page visits, interactions, approximate location
Advertising Google Ads, LinkedIn Ads, Meta Ads or similar platforms Campaign measurement, remarketing, conversion tracking Cookie identifiers, conversion data, page visits, campaign data
CRM and sales HubSpot, Pipedrive, Notion, Airtable or similar systems Lead management, client follow-up, project tracking, sales process Contact details, company details, project notes, sales status
Booking Calendly, Google Calendar, Microsoft Bookings or similar tools Scheduling calls and meetings Name, email, company, meeting details, time zone
Cloud storage Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Dropbox or similar tools Document storage, project work, collaboration Project files, business documents, communication data
AI and automation OpenAI, Anthropic, Make, Zapier, n8n or similar tools AI-assisted work, automation, research, content, workflow support Only data needed for the specific task, preferably minimised or anonymised
Accounting Bookkeeping software, accountant, payment provider Invoices, administration, tax obligations Billing details, invoices, payment status, tax records

11. AI tools and automation

Booming Venture works with AI, automation and growth systems. In some cases, we may use AI tools to support content creation, research, analysis, marketing workflows, meeting summaries, proposal drafting, campaign planning, reporting and internal productivity.

11.1 How we use AI responsibly

When we use AI tools, we aim to apply data minimisation. This means we only use the information that is necessary for the task.

We do not intentionally enter sensitive personal data into AI tools unless this is necessary, appropriate, legally allowed and covered by suitable safeguards.

When we process client data with AI tools, we aim to use professional tools with appropriate security, contractual terms and data protection measures.

11.2 No fully automated legal or significant decisions

We do not use AI to make decisions about individuals that have legal or similarly significant effects without human review.

11.3 Client data and AI tools

If client data needs to be processed with AI tools for a project, we assess what data is needed, which tool is appropriate, whether a processor agreement or other safeguards are required, and whether anonymisation or pseudonymisation is possible.

12. Embedded content and third-party websites

Our website may contain embedded content, such as videos, maps, social posts, forms, calendars, podcasts or articles.

Embedded content from other websites behaves as if you visited that external website directly. These external websites may collect data, use cookies, place tracking technologies and monitor your interaction with their content.

We are not responsible for the privacy practices of external websites. Always read the privacy policy of the external provider.

13. International data transfers

Some tools or service providers may process data outside the European Economic Area.

Where this happens, we take appropriate safeguards, such as:

  • Using providers with appropriate data protection measures
  • Using standard contractual clauses where required
  • Checking transfer risks where needed
  • Limiting the data shared
  • Choosing EU-based processing where practical
  • Using professional business accounts instead of unmanaged consumer tools where possible

14. How long we keep personal data

We do not keep personal data longer than necessary. The retention period depends on the type of data, the purpose of processing and legal obligations.

Data type Retention period
Contact form submissions Up to 24 months after last contact, unless needed longer for a request, project, legal claim or administration
Sales and proposal communication Up to 36 months after last meaningful contact, unless there is a client relationship or legal reason to keep it longer
Client project data Up to 7 years after the end of the client relationship, unless a shorter period is agreed or a longer period is legally needed
Contracts, invoices and accounting records At least 7 years because of Dutch tax administration rules
Newsletter data Until you unsubscribe or the list is cleaned
Unsubscribe records As long as needed to make sure we do not email you again
Cookie consent records As long as needed to prove consent and manage preferences
Website analytics data As short as reasonably possible, depending on the tool settings
Security logs Usually up to 12 months, unless needed longer for investigation, fraud prevention or security
Comments, if enabled Until removed or no longer needed
Job, supplier or collaboration inquiries Up to 12 months unless you agree to longer retention or a business relationship starts

We may keep data longer if this is necessary for legal claims, disputes, fraud prevention, security investigations or legal obligations.

15. How we protect your data

We take appropriate technical and organisational measures to protect personal data.

These may include:

  • Secure hosting
  • SSL encryption
  • Access control
  • Strong passwords
  • Two-factor authentication where possible
  • Limited access to personal data
  • Regular software updates
  • Spam and security protection
  • Backups
  • Processor agreements
  • Secure cloud tools
  • Internal data minimisation
  • Deletion of unnecessary data
  • Careful handling of client data

No system is completely secure, but we work to reduce risks and protect data properly.

16. Data breaches

If a personal data breach happens, we will assess the risk and take appropriate action.

Where required, we will report a breach to the Dutch Data Protection Authority without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours after becoming aware of it.

If a breach is likely to result in a high risk to your rights and freedoms, we will also inform affected individuals without undue delay.

17. Your privacy rights

You have rights under the General Data Protection Regulation. These include:

  • Right to access your personal data
  • Right to correct inaccurate data
  • Right to delete your data
  • Right to restrict processing
  • Right to object to processing
  • Right to data portability
  • Right to withdraw consent
  • Right to complain to a supervisory authority

You can exercise your rights by contacting us at info@boomingventure.com.

We may need to verify your identity before handling your request. We aim to respond within one month.

17.1 Withdrawing consent

If we process your data based on consent, you can withdraw your consent at any time.

For example, you can unsubscribe from marketing emails, change cookie preferences, or contact us to withdraw consent for a specific processing activity.

Withdrawing consent does not affect processing that happened before consent was withdrawn.

17.2 Objection to direct marketing

You can object to direct marketing at any time. If you object, we will stop using your personal data for direct marketing.

You can use the unsubscribe link in emails or contact us directly.

18. Complaints

If you have a privacy complaint, please contact us first so we can try to solve it.

You also have the right to file a complaint with the Dutch Data Protection Authority.

Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens
Website: https://www.autoriteitpersoonsgegevens.nl

19. Children

Our website and services are intended for business users and are not directed at children.

We do not knowingly collect personal data from children.

If you believe we have collected personal data from a child, contact us so we can delete it where required.

20. Changes to this Privacy Policy

We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time.

The latest version will always be available on our website. The date at the top shows when the policy was last updated.

If the changes are significant, we may notify users through the website or by email where appropriate.

21. Implementation checklist for Booming Venture

This checklist is part of the practical privacy setup. The policy only works properly if the website and internal process match it.

21.1 Cookie setup

  • Use a cookie banner with Accept and Reject on the first layer
  • Make rejecting cookies as easy as accepting cookies
  • Block marketing cookies before consent
  • Block advertising pixels before consent
  • Block non-essential third-party embeds before consent where needed
  • Keep proof of consent
  • Allow users to change or withdraw consent

21.2 Tool audit

Check every active tool on the website and in operations:

  • WordPress
  • Hosting provider
  • Theme and plugins
  • Contact Form 7 or other form tools
  • Brevo or email marketing software
  • Google Analytics
  • Google Tag Manager
  • Google Ads
  • LinkedIn Insight Tag
  • Meta Pixel
  • Microsoft Clarity
  • Hotjar
  • Calendly or booking widgets
  • HubSpot or CRM tools
  • reCAPTCHA, Akismet or spam tools
  • YouTube, Vimeo or Google Maps embeds
  • AI tools and automation tools

21.3 Processor agreements

Make sure processor agreements are in place where required, especially for:

  • Hosting
  • Email marketing
  • CRM
  • Analytics
  • Forms
  • Cloud storage
  • Automation tools
  • AI tools used with client data
  • Bookkeeping and accounting tools

21.4 Internal privacy register

Keep a simple internal register with:

  • Processing activity
  • Purpose
  • Data categories
  • Legal basis
  • Processor
  • Storage location
  • Retention period
  • Security measures
  • Whether consent is needed

21.5 WordPress risk reduction

  • Disable comments if not needed
  • Disable user registration if not needed
  • Remove unused plugins
  • Update plugins and theme regularly
  • Use two-factor authentication for admin users
  • Limit admin access
  • Use a backup and security plugin
  • Check that forms do not subscribe people to newsletters without separate consent

Do not say that data is 100 percent secure. The safer and more accurate wording is: we take appropriate technical and organisational measures.
